messages:
rachel: Heads-up from today's CP split spike: customers on private CP + peered VPCs are seeing intermittent private-endpoint auth failures during peering route churn. Root cause looks like cert propagation delays to regional relays.

devon: Can you clarify: is the cert the one we generate for the endpoint or customer certs for egress allowlist?

rachel: The endpoint cert (our controlplane cert) that relays use to terminate mTLS. We push rotation bundles to edge relays after a CP rollout; some relays lag ~30-90s which causes client TLS verify failures while routes switch.

ajay: Is this specific to peering attach/detach events, or also during scale-up of relays?

rachel: Mostly during peering re-attachments and AZ failover where we reassign route targets to different relay instances. The flow: route flips -> client hits new relay -> relay doesn't yet have latest cert bundle -> mutual TLS fails -> client retries and falls back to regional NAT (if configured) -> downstream allowlist mismatch.

kumar: Two high-level options: 1) pre-propagate certs to candidate relays before route flip (prep phase), or 2) change handshake semantics to SNI passthrough for upgrade window so we avoid termination mismatch. Tradeoffs?

devon: Pre-propagation keeps mTLS semantics but complicates rollout ordering and requires reliable list of candidate relays. SNI passthrough reduces our ability to inspect requests at relay and we lose certain tracing/ratelimiting hooks.

emma: For Private deployments customers who run CP in their VPC, pre-propagation might be impossible if they manage relays. We need distinct handling for Hosted vs Private.

ajay: What about a hybrid: pre-propagate when we control relays, and for customer-managed relays expose a lightweight handshake shim: a short-lived bootstrap cert that is accepted during a 2-minute window post-route-change, then we rotate to full cert.

kumar: That still requires cert sync to be robust: we need an idempotent push and an acknowledgment channel. Maybe extend the relay control protocol with cert_version and ack. If ack missing, we pause route promotion.

rachel: I like the ack idea. Proposed flow: (A) controller determines candidate relay set, (B) push new cert bundle with version tag, (C) wait for >= N relays to ack (configurable, default 80%), (D) flip routes. If ack threshold not met within timeout, revert or fallback to short SNI passthrough for affected tenants.

devon: Need to measure expected lag. Current worst-case seems ~90s; set ack timeout to 120s by default and make it adjustable per-customer. Also export metric cert_push_latency and relay_ack_rate.

emma: For Private customers we should provide an opt-in "zero-downtime cert sync" helper that they can run in their infra: small agent that accepts bundle and immediately writes it to relay. Doc that this is required for strict SLAs.

ajay: Also, edge case: what if ACKs come from old relay set that will be decommissioned immediately after flip? We must bind ack identity to instance-id and route membership. Controller should compute intersection of candidate list and ackers.

kumar: Good catch. Controller must snapshot candidate set and only count ACKs from those snapshotted identities. Logging: include cert_version + snapshot_id in controller logs and relay acknowledgments for audit.

infra-bot: infra-bot: Proposed alert rule: \"relay_cert_ack_rate_low\" when ack_rate < 0.8 over 2m. Pager: eng-oncall + neteng.

rachel: UX: in Console show a rollout stepper that displays cert_push status per-region with red/amber/green, and show a banner if we fall back to SNI passthrough for a tenant. That helps CS and security teams.

devon: Add tracing tags: cert_version and relay_snapshot_id to spans for controlplane handoffs, and include them in access logs for debugging.

emma: Security note: the bootstrap short-lived cert must be limited: single-use per-route-flip and short TTL (e.g., 2m). Ensure KMS audit records include which controller issued it.

ajay: Implementation tasks I see: 1) extend relay control API to accept cert bundles + version, 2) controller pre-propagation flow + ack logic, 3) Console rollout UI + metrics, 4) opt-in helper for Private deployments, 5) fallback SNI passthrough mode and policy, 6) docs & customer comms.

rachel: I'll draft a follow-up RFC titled \"relay-cert-prepropagation-ack\" with sequence diagrams and rollout plan. Quick mitigation: for impacted customers we temporarily enable per-tenant static egress IP via NAT relay and coordinate IP allowlist updates.

devon: Admin troubleshooting CLI snippet (helpful during incident):

```
# list vpc endpoints and tags for relay membership
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=tag:relay-snapshot,Values=*" --query 'VpcEndpoints[].[VpcEndpointId,State,Tags]' --output table
```

kumar: Also document how to repro locally: spin up 3 relays, simulate cert push with missing acks and assert route flip stalls. Add integration test.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New runbook entry created: \"relay-cert-ack-fallback\". Refer: 1725820001.

emma: Can we also add a per-tenant override to prefer SNI passthrough always? Some customers may prioritize no-inspection mode. We'll add a tenant flag but default to termination.

rachel: Yes, tenant-level flag makes sense. Default: termination with prepropagation. Override: passthrough. We'll capture in RFC.

devon: OK great. Timeline? If RFC lands this week we can spike next sprint and target canary next month.

rachel: Sounds good. I'll post RFC draft in #architecture by EOD and tag network + security. Thanks everyone.
